# To whoever finds this

I folded every thought I could not say out loud, then left it on the table.

Read it slowly.

— A.

do not forget
to water
the plants

— me

# SNOW ARRIVES EARLY
The first flakes fell over the market square before breakfast, and by noon the bakers had sold out of everything warm.

The weather office promises a clear week after that.

sunday, early

bought the good bread.
the bird came back to the window.

write to the cousins.

Dear reader,

this sheet was typed on a machine that sticks on every third letter. Forgive the spacing.

monday night

could not sleep again.
made a list of things to fix tomorrow.

do not read the rest.

# CONTINUOUS FORM - LOG
UNIT: 04
STATUS: AWAITING SIGNATURE

READING 01 ..... 0412
READING 02 ..... 0413
READING 03 ..... ERROR

# THE GRAND THEATRE
EVENING PERFORMANCE
ROW C - SEAT 12

admit one

# INTERNAL MEMO
TO: [[the whole team]]
FROM: the front desk
RE: the plant by the window

Please water it on Fridays. [[Nobody remembers who started this.]]

Further notes next week.

# FOG STAYS FOR A THIRD DAY
Residents woke to the same thick fog that has covered the harbor since Monday. Ferries kept to their schedule, guided only by the lighthouse.

The weather office expects clear skies by the weekend.

remember:
buy stamps
and the good pencils
summer, last day

Dear friend,

I kept this letter in a drawer for a whole year before sending it.

Read it, then let it go.

— yours

Dear reader,

the edges of this page have been through a lot. So have I.

— A.

This letter survived the fire.

Mostly.

The coffee was on the table before the letter was.

I still wrote it anyway.

It rained on the window all night.
Some of the ink ran away.

The rest is true.

Sorry about the fingerprints.
I was reading it on the stairs.

Written long ago, and kept well.

Turn it over for the date.

I will ~~never~~{always} forget how the lake looked in the morning.

— A.

This note burns after reading.

Go on, read it once.

hiddenInk: the real message is written under the light, very small
text:
Nothing to see here.

Keep reading.

Dear friend,

this envelope has been sealed since the autumn. Open it when you have a quiet hour.

— yours

The edges went brown before I could read the last line.

The middle is still here.

Dinner ran late.

The wine marked the corner of the page.

The pen leaked on the way home.

The words are still under the blot.

Kept in a box in the attic for forty years.

The brown spots are the years.

I taped the corners to the fridge.

Now the tape has yellowed along with the note.

Received, filed and forgotten.

The stamp is the only part that stayed in order.

This was written in blue ink.

The sun took almost all of the blue.

Held together with a galvanized staple.

The fiber shows the mark.

An oil stain soaked through the fibers.

You can almost see the other side.

Corner folded over to mark the page.

A habit that became permanent.

Wetted by mist and dried in the breeze.

The surface kept its wave.

Carried folded inside a pocket for months.

A grid of micro-creases.

The fire started in one corner and climbed slowly.

The rest of the sheet is still readable.

The fire walked along the whole edge.

The middle of the text is still intact.
A hole burned out of the middle, and the words around it can still be read.

A few embers landed here and there.

Each one left a small mark.
